steps_basic.title: Choose your pet sprite
steps_basic.instruction: Open Scratch and choose a Pet sprite from the sprite library (or keep the cat and rename it 'Pet').
steps_basic.hint: Click the sprite icon in the bottom right to add a new sprite from the library.

steps_basic.title: Add click event
steps_basic.instruction: Click on your Pet sprite to select it. Then drag 'when this sprite clicked' from Events into the coding area.
steps_basic.hint: Look in the Events category (yellow blocks) for the 'when this sprite clicked' block.

steps_basic.title: Make your pet talk
steps_basic.instruction: Add a 'say' block so your pet says 'Hello! I am your pet!' for 2 seconds when clicked.
steps_basic.hint: Find the 'say [ ] for ( ) seconds' block in the Looks category (purple).
steps_basic.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hello! I am your pet!] for (2) seconds

steps_basic.title: Test your pet
steps_basic.instruction: Click on your pet sprite on the stage. Does it say hello? If yes, mark this step as Done!
steps_basic.hint: Click directly on the pet in the stage area (the big white area on the right).
steps_basic.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hello! I am your pet!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Start fresh
steps_standard.instruction: You've unlocked Standard level! Start with your Basic code, or create a new Pet sprite if needed.
steps_standard.hint: Make sure you have the Basic level code working first.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
say [Hello! I am your pet!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Create a mood variable
steps_standard.instruction: Go to Variables and make a new variable called 'mood' (for all sprites).
steps_standard.hint: Click Variables → Make a Variable → type 'mood' → OK

steps_standard.title: Set happy mood on start
steps_standard.instruction: Add 'when green flag clicked' event. Set mood to 'happy' and switch to a happy costume.
steps_standard.hint: You may need to add or duplicate costumes in the Costumes tab first.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when green flag clicked
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]

steps_standard.title: Make pet get hungry over time
steps_standard.instruction: Add a 'forever' loop. Inside: wait 10 seconds, set mood to 'hungry', switch to hungry costume, say 'I'm hungry!' for 2 seconds.
steps_standard.hint: Control → forever. Put all the blocks inside the forever loop.
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when green flag clicked
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]
forever
  wait (10) seconds
  set [mood v] to [hungry]
  switch costume to [hungry v]
  say [I'm hungry!] for (2) seconds

steps_standard.title: Add a Food button sprite
steps_standard.instruction: Add a new sprite for Food (use a food icon or draw one). This will be your feeding button.
steps_standard.hint: Click the sprite icon in bottom right → Choose a food sprite or paint one.

steps_standard.title: Food button broadcasts FEED
steps_standard.instruction: Click the Food sprite. Add 'when this sprite clicked' and 'broadcast FEED'.
steps_standard.hint: Events → when this sprite clicked. Events → broadcast → New message → type 'FEED'
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
broadcast [FEED v]

steps_standard.title: Pet receives FEED and becomes happy
steps_standard.instruction: Click Pet sprite. Add 'when I receive FEED', set mood to happy, switch costume to happy, say 'Yum!' for 1 second.
steps_standard.hint: Make sure you're coding on the Pet sprite, not the Food sprite!
steps_standard.blocks_text:
when I receive [FEED v]
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]
say [Yum!] for (1) seconds

steps_standard.title: Test your smart pet
steps_standard.instruction: Click green flag. Wait 10 seconds for pet to get hungry. Click Food button. Does pet become happy? Mark Done!
steps_standard.hint: The pet should cycle: happy → hungry (after 10s) → happy (when fed) → hungry again...

steps_advanced.title: Start with Standard code
steps_advanced.instruction: You've unlocked Advanced level! You'll add an energy system and sleep button. Make sure your Standard code is working.
steps_advanced.hint: You should have: Pet with mood variable, Food button that broadcasts FEED, and hungry/happy system.

steps_advanced.title: Create energy variable
steps_advanced.instruction: Make a new variable called 'energy' (for all sprites). This tracks your pet's energy level.
steps_advanced.hint: Variables → Make a Variable → type 'energy' → OK

steps_advanced.title: Set starting energy
steps_advanced.instruction: In Pet's 'when green flag clicked', add 'set energy to 10' at the start.
steps_advanced.hint: Put it right after the green flag block, before setting mood.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when green flag clicked
set [energy v] to (10)
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]
forever
  wait (10) seconds
  set [mood v] to [hungry]
  switch costume to [hungry v]
  say [I'm hungry!] for (2) seconds

steps_advanced.title: Energy decreases over time
steps_advanced.instruction: Inside the Pet's forever loop, add another loop that runs every 5 seconds and changes energy by -1.
steps_advanced.hint: You can nest loops! Or add a separate 'forever' script. Variables → change [energy] by (-1)
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when green flag clicked
set [energy v] to (10)
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]
forever
  wait (5) seconds
  change [energy v] by (-1)

steps_advanced.title: Pet gets sleepy when energy is low
steps_advanced.instruction: Add an 'if then' block: if energy < 3, set mood to 'sleepy', switch to sleepy costume, say 'So sleepy...'
steps_advanced.hint: Operators → (energy) < (3). Control → if then. Put inside the energy loop.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when green flag clicked
set [energy v] to (10)
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]
forever
  wait (5) seconds
  change [energy v] by (-1)
  if <(energy) < (3)> then
    set [mood v] to [sleepy]
    switch costume to [sleepy v]
    say [So sleepy...] for (2) seconds

steps_advanced.title: Add Sleep button sprite
steps_advanced.instruction: Add a new sprite for Sleep (use a bed icon or draw a pillow/moon). This will restore energy.
steps_advanced.hint: Click sprite icon → Choose or paint a sleep-related sprite.

steps_advanced.title: Sleep button broadcasts SLEEP
steps_advanced.instruction: Click Sleep sprite. Add 'when this sprite clicked' and 'broadcast SLEEP'.
steps_advanced.hint: Events → when this sprite clicked. Events → broadcast → New message → type 'SLEEP'
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when this sprite clicked
broadcast [SLEEP v]

steps_advanced.title: Pet receives SLEEP and recovers energy
steps_advanced.instruction: Click Pet sprite. Add 'when I receive SLEEP', set energy to 10, set mood to happy, switch costume to happy.
steps_advanced.blocks_text:
when I receive [SLEEP v]
set [energy v] to (10)
set [mood v] to [happy]
switch costume to [happy v]

steps_advanced.title: Optional: Show energy meter
steps_advanced.instruction: Right-click the energy variable on stage and choose 'large readout' or 'slider' to display it visually.
steps_advanced.hint: This helps players see the energy level as it changes.

steps_advanced.title: Test the complete pet system
steps_advanced.instruction: Click green flag. Watch as pet gets hungry, then sleepy. Feed it and let it sleep. Does everything work? Mark Done!
steps_advanced.hint: Your pet should now have: hunger (10s cycle), energy (5s drain), feeding, and sleeping!
